title_en: Level 8 checkpoint: a recorded lesson, and every kind of text
q_en: Can I read a lesson that was spoken and written down, and tell what kind of text any page is?
q_ar: هَلْ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ دَرْسًا قِيلَ ثُمَّ كُتِبَ، وَأَنْ أَعْرِفَ نَوْعَ أَيِّ نَصٍّ؟
not_yet: Pages of every kind without any help: that is reading, and it comes from reading every day.
The texts of the world around you (news, forms, prices): Level 9.
Checking a ḥadīth or a quotation yourself in the books.
not_yet_ar: صَفَحَاتٌ مِنْ كُلِّ نَوْعٍ بِلَا مُسَاعَدَةٍ: هَذِهِ هِيَ الْقِرَاءَةُ، وَتَأْتِي بِالْقِرَاءَةِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.
نُصُوصُ الْعَالَمِ حَوْلَكَ (الْأَخْبَارُ وَالِاسْتِمَارَاتُ وَالْأَسْعَارُ): الْمُسْتَوَى التَّاسِعُ.
التَّأَكُّدُ بِنَفْسِكَ مِنْ حَدِيثٍ أَوْ نَقْلٍ فِي الْكُتُبِ.

sents: وَقَدْ سَجَّلْنَا هَذَا الدَّرْسَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
And we have recorded this lesson in the mosque.
Then the student wrote what he heard.
And what prevents you from remembrance?

lines: Which little words open the sentences: وَقَدْ، ثُمَّ، فَـ، وَ?
Who is speaking: “I”, “we” or “he”? What ending shows it?
مَنِ الْمُتَكَلِّمُ: «أَنَا» أَمْ «نَحْنُ» أَمْ «هُوَ»؟ أَيُّ نِهَايَةٍ تَدُلُّ؟
The third sentence asks a question. Does it want an answer? The last has a past verb. Is it news?
الْجُمْلَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ سُؤَالٌ. هَلْ تُرِيدُ جَوَابًا؟ وَالْأَخِيرَةُ فِعْلُهَا مَاضٍ. هَلْ هِيَ خَبَرٌ؟

slides.why: A student answers the question “And what prevents you?” with “The market.” Wrong! The writer does not want an answer. It is a rhetorical question: it means “Nothing should prevent you.”
slides.why_ar: أَجَابَ طَالِبٌ عَنْ «وَمَاذَا يَمْنَعُكَ؟» بِقَوْلِهِ «السُّوقُ». خَطَأٌ! الْكَاتِبُ لَا يَطْلُبُ جَوَابًا. هَذَا سُؤَالٌ بَلَاغِيٌّ، مَعْنَاهُ: لَا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يَمْنَعَكَ شَيْءٌ.

slides.head_en: A lesson written down: a preface
lines: وَقَدْ سَجَّلْنَا دُرُوسًا تَتَعَلَّقُ بِهَذَا الشَّأْنِ بِعُنْوَانِ (مَمْلَكَةُ الْقَلْبِ وَالْأَعْضَاءِ)
(Mamlakat al-Qalb:) We have recorded lessons on this matter under the title "The Kingdom of the Heart and the Limbs".
فَخَرَجَتْ تِلْكَ الدُّرُوسُ مِنَ الْإِلْقَاءِ وَالتَّسْجِيلِ الصَّوْتِيِّ إِلَى هَذِهِ الْكِتَابَةِ
So those lessons have come out of delivery and sound recording into this writing,
جَعَلَ اللهُ كُلَّ ذَلِكَ خَالِصًا لِوَجْهِهِ الْكَرِيمِ، وَكَتَبَ بِهِ النَّفْعَ الْعَظِيمَ
May God make all of that purely for His noble sake, and write great benefit by it.
slides.source: Mamlakat al-Qalb wa-l-Aʿḍāʾ of al-Ḥabīb ʿUmar b. Ḥafīẓ (the author’s preface; three lines)

sections.name: A
sections.en: A lesson written down: four lines of a book by al-Ḥabīb ʿUmar. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: فَيَجِبُ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ نَصِيبٌ مِنَ الذِّكْرِ, وَأَوْلَى الذِّكْرِ تِلَاوَةُ كِتَابِ اللهِ
(Isʿāf:) So a believer must have a share of remembrance of God, and the best remembrance is reciting God's Book.
فَلَا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يُهْمِلَهُ وَتَمُرُّ عَلَيْهِ الْأَيَّامُ لَا يَتَدَبَّرُ شَيْئًا مِنْ كَلَامِ رَبِّهِ جَلَّ جَلَالُهُ
So he should not neglect it and let days pass without reflecting on anything of the words of his Lord, great is His majesty.
ثُمَّ لِيَأْخُذْ نَصِيبًا مِنْ ذِكْرِ الصَّبَاحِ وَالْمَسَاءِ مِمَّا وَرَدَ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ مُحَمَّدٍ
Then let him take a share of the morning and evening remembrance reported from the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ,
وَمَاذَا يَمْنَعُكَ مِنْهُ عِنْدَ دُخُولِ الْبَيْتِ؟
and what prevents you from it when you enter the house?
sections.source: Isʿāf Ṭālibī Riḍā al-Khallāq of al-Ḥabīb ʿUmar b. Ḥafīẓ (four lines)
sections.cite: ʿUmar b. Muḥammad b. Sālim b. Ḥafīẓ, Isʿāf Ṭālibī Riḍā al-Khallāq bi-Bayān Makārim al-Akhlāq, 1st ed. 1424 AH / 2003, Markaz al-Nūr li-l-Dirāsāt wa-l-Abḥāth, Tarīm, distributed by Dār al-Faqīh, Ṣanʿāʾ (deposit no. 181 of 2003) (TLNOOR id 729, a digital epub), the section marked 6.1 (the epub gives no printed page numbers): four consecutive lines, the whole of the quotation from this book in the course (in copyright: ≤ 4 lines). The epub text is only partly vowelled; the course completes the vowels (vowelled for learners), keeping every letter. One reading to report: the epub has تمرُّ (ḍamma) in وتمرُّ عليه الأيامُ; the course keeps it. The epub text ends النبي محمدٍ with no salutation; the course keeps the Arabic exactly and prints ﷺ in the English. In the student book the section is vowelled.
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults and older students; children may skip them. The vowels are completed for learners: the printed book has few of them.

items.en: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
items.model: A book of good character written by a living teacher, in the style of a talk written down: it speaks to “you” and asks a question. It is from Isʿāf Ṭālibī Riḍā al-Khallāq by al-Ḥabīb ʿUmar b. Ḥafīẓ.

items.en: Which text type is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ هَذَا؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: Contemporary prose, a lesson written down: وَمَاذَا يَمْنَعُكَ؟ speaks to the reader; there are no matn words, no chain, no verse and no counting.

items.en: Line 1: what must a believer have? What is the best remembrance?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ١: مَاذَا يَجِبُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ؟ وَمَا أَوْلَى الذِّكْرِ؟
items.model: A share of remembrance (نَصِيبٌ مِنَ الذِّكْرِ); the best is reciting the Book of God.

items.en: What does يَجِبُ tell you? Which text type uses this word most?
items.ar_q: عَلَى مَاذَا تَدُلُّ كَلِمَةُ «يَجِبُ»؟ فِي أَيِّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ تُسْتَعْمَلُ كَثِيرًا؟
items.model: “It is obligatory.” Fiqh (rulings).

items.en: Line 2: what should he not do, and what must not pass over him?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٢: مَاذَا لَا يَنْبَغِي لَهُ؟ وَمَاذَا لَا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يَمُرَّ عَلَيْهِ؟
items.model: He should not neglect it (the Book of God); days should not pass without his reflecting on any of the words of his Lord.

items.en: Whom does this phrase describe? Why is it written?
items.ar_q: مَنِ الَّذِي يَصِفُهُ هَذَا التَّعْبِيرُ؟ لِمَاذَا يُكْتَبُ؟
items.model: His Lord: it is a phrase of respect after His name: “great is His majesty”.

items.en: Line 3: what else should he take a share of? Where does it come from?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٣: مِمَّ يَأْخُذُ نَصِيبًا أَيْضًا؟ مِنْ أَيْنَ جَاءَ؟
items.model: The morning and evening remembrance that is reported from the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ.

items.en: Is the writer waiting for you to answer? What is he doing?
items.ar_q: هَلْ يَنْتَظِرُ الْكَاتِبُ جَوَابَكَ؟ مَاذَا يَفْعَلُ؟
items.model: No. It is a rhetorical question: he is gently telling the reader that nothing should prevent him.

items.en: What does the ـهُ in مِنْهُ stand for?
items.ar_q: إِلَى مَاذَا تَرْجِعُ الْهَاءُ فِي «مِنْهُ»؟
items.model: The remembrance (الذِّكْر) of line 3.

items.en: Find the little word and the noun: what does it mean?
items.ar_q: جِدِ الْحَرْفَ وَالِاسْمَ: مَا مَعْنَاهُمَا؟
items.model: عِنْدَ + دُخُولِ: “at the entering of (the house)”: when you enter the house.

items.en: Root hunt: what is the root of الْأَيَّامُ?
items.ar_q: صَيْدُ الْجُذُورِ: مَا جَذْرُ «الْأَيَّامُ»؟
items.model: ي و م: day.

items.en: ★ The line begins فَيَجِبُ. What does فَـ do, and why does a book of this kind give an obligation?
items.ar_q: ★ مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ «فَـ» فِي «فَيَجِبُ»؟ لِمَاذَا يَذْكُرُ كِتَابٌ كَهَذَا وَاجِبًا؟
items.model: فَـ joins the sentence to what comes before it, as in talk: “so it is obligatory …”. The author teaches how to live, so he states what a believer owes.

items.en: ★ Compare this page with the preface on the slides. Name two things the two pages share.
items.ar_q: ★ قَارِنْ بَيْنَ هَذِهِ الصَّفْحَةِ وَالْمُقَدِّمَةِ فِي الشَّرَائِحِ. اُذْكُرْ شَيْئَيْنِ تَشْتَرِكَانِ فِيهِمَا.
items.model: Both are spoken style written down; both use little words to chain the sentences and an invocation of God (جَعَلَ اللهُ … ; جَلَّ جَلَالُهُ).

sections.name: B
sections.en: A short text: the recording. It is printed without vowels, as in a book for students. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ فِي الْبَيْتِ وَفَتَحَ تَسْجِيلًا لِدَرْسٍ سَمِعَهُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
At night Ahmad sat with his father in the house and opened a recording of a lesson he had heard in the mosque.
وَقَالَ الْمُعَلِّمُ فِي التَّسْجِيلِ: وَقَدْ سَمِعْتُمْ مِنَّا الْيَوْمَ دَرْسًا فِي هَذَا الشَّأْنِ.
And the teacher said in the recording: You have heard from us today a lesson on this matter.
ثُمَّ قَالَ: اُكْتُبْ يَا أَحْمَدُ مَا سَمِعْتَ، ثُمَّ اقْرَأْهُ فِي الْبَيْتِ.
Then he said: Write, Ahmad, what you heard, then read it at home.
وَمَاذَا يَمْنَعُكَ مِنَ الذِّكْرِ فِي اللَّيْلِ؟
And what prevents you from remembrance at night?
فَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ مَا سَمِعَ فِي كِتَابِهِ.
So Ahmad wrote what he heard in his book.
ثُمَّ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ: هَذَا الشَّأْنُ عَظِيمٌ، وَقَدْ حَفِظْتُ مِنْهُ نَصِيبًا.
Then he said to his father: This matter is great, and I have memorised a share of it.
فَقَالَ أَبُوهُ: جَعَلَ اللَّهُ ذَلِكَ خَالِصًا لِوَجْهِهِ الْكَرِيمِ.
His father said: May Allah make that purely for His noble sake.
وَنَامَ أَحْمَدُ وَالدَّرْسُ مَحْفُوظٌ فِي كِتَابِهِ.
And Ahmad slept, with the lesson kept safe in his book.
sections.teacher_note: This paragraph is printed without vowels on purpose: the key has them. The two ★ rows are for adults and older students; children may skip them.

items.en: Where does Ahmad sit, and what does he open? (line 1)
items.ar_q: أَيْنَ يَجْلِسُ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَمَاذَا يَفْتَحُ؟
items.model: In the house, with his father; he opens a recording of a lesson he heard in the mosque.

items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
items.model: And the teacher said in the recording: You have heard from us today a lesson on this matter.

items.en: What does قَدْ add here? Who is “you”?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا تُفِيدُ «قَدْ»؟ مَنْ «أَنْتُمْ»؟
items.model: قَدْ + past verb: “already, indeed”. The ending shows “you” (plural): the listeners.

items.en: What two things does the teacher ask Ahmad to do? (line 3)
items.ar_q: مَاذَا يَطْلُبُ الْمُعَلِّمُ مِنْ أَحْمَدَ؟
options: He wrote what he heard in his book.
The second comes after the first: first write, then read.
To write what he heard, then to read it at home.
items.answer: To write what he heard, then to read it at home.
items.model: To write what he heard, then to read it at home.

items.en: What does ثُمَّ show about the two commands?
items.ar_q: عَلَى مَاذَا تَدُلُّ «ثُمَّ»؟
options: He wrote what he heard in his book.
The second comes after the first: first write, then read.
To write what he heard, then to read it at home.
items.answer: The second comes after the first: first write, then read.
items.model: The second comes after the first: first write, then read.

items.en: Read the question aloud with its vowels. Is it a real question?
items.ar_q: اِقْرَأِ السُّؤَالَ بِحَرَكَاتِهِ. هَلْ هُوَ سُؤَالٌ حَقِيقِيٌّ؟
items.model: وَمَاذَا يَمْنَعُكَ مِنَ الذِّكْرِ فِي اللَّيْلِ؟ No: it encourages him; nothing should prevent him.

items.en: What did Ahmad do after the recording? (line 5)
items.ar_q: مَاذَا فَعَلَ أَحْمَدُ بَعْدَ التَّسْجِيلِ؟
options: To write what he heard, then to read it at home.
The second comes after the first: first write, then read.
He wrote what he heard in his book.
items.answer: He wrote what he heard in his book.
items.model: He wrote what he heard in his book.

items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ السَّادِسَ.
items.model: Then he said to his father: This matter is great, and I have memorised a share of it.

items.ar: جعل الله ذلك خالصًا لوجهه الكريم
items.en: Is this telling you what happened, or is it a wish? How do you know?
items.ar_q: هَلْ تُخْبِرُ هَذِهِ الْجُمْلَةُ عَمَّا حَدَثَ أَمْ هِيَ دُعَاءٌ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: A wish: “May Allah make that purely for His noble sake.” The doer is Allah and the speaker asks for good.

items.en: Find the word that means “preserved, kept safe”. What is its root?
items.ar_q: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي تَعْنِي «فِي أَمَانٍ، لَمْ يَضِعْ». مَا جَذْرُهَا؟
options: To write what he heard, then to read it at home.
The second comes after the first: first write, then read.
He wrote what he heard in his book.
items.model: مَحْفُوظ; root ح ف ظ.

items.en: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: A short story: people, a place, a night; the recording inside it is spoken style written down.

items.en: ★ The teacher in the recording says “from us” (مِنَّا) but speaks to one boy in line 3. Why do both appear?
items.ar_q: ★ يَقُولُ الْمُعَلِّمُ «مِنَّا» ثُمَّ يُخَاطِبُ وَلَدًا وَاحِدًا. لِمَاذَا يَجْتَمِعَانِ؟
items.model: “We” is the style of a teacher or author speaking for himself and his circle; he then turns to one listener, as speech does.

sections.name: C
sections.en: Unseen lines. Each comes from a different kind of text. Say which kind, and how you know. (The vowels are in the lines; some words are glossed.)
lines: كَقَوْلِهِ : الْحَجُّ عَرَفَةُ أَيْ عِمَادُهُ وَمُعْظَمُهُ عَرَفَةُ
like his saying, "Ḥajj is ʿArafa", that is, its pillar and greatest part is ʿArafa.
وَمَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
And whoever takes a road seeking knowledge on it, God makes easy for him by it a road to Paradise.
وَلَا يُسَنُّ رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ فِي غَيْرِ هَذِهِ الْمَوَاضِعِ الْأَرْبَعَةِ
And raising the hands is not recommended anywhere but these four places.
وَمَا يَسْتَحِيلُ عَلَيْهِ تَعَالَى وَعَلَيْهِمْ، وَمَا يَجُوزُ فِي حَقِّهِ تَعَالَى وَفِي حَقِّهِمْ.
and what is impossible for Him and for them, and what is possible for Him and for them.
يَا ذَا الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ، أَمِتْنَا عَلَى دِينِ الْإِسْلَامِ (7 مَرَّاتٍ)
O Possessor of majesty and honour, let us die in the religion of Islam (7 times).
فَأَرْسَلَ إِلَيْهِمْ أَشْرَفَ خَلْقِهِ وَأَجَلَّ عَبِيدِهِ رَحْمَه
So He sent to them, as a mercy, the noblest of His creation and the greatest of His servants.
فَمِنْكَ كُلُّ خِيرَةٍ * وَكُلُّ نِعْمَةٍ بِنَا
From You is every good and every blessing upon us.
وَهُوَ يُوَافِقُ السَّنَةَ الْأُولَى مِنْ حَادِثَةِ الْفِيلِ
which corresponds to the first year after the Elephant incident.
وَقَرَأَ عَلَيْهِ فِي الْحَدِيثِ وَالتَّفْسِيرِ وَالتَّصَوُّفِ وَالْعَرَبِيَّةِ
and read with him in ḥadīth, Qurʾān commentary, Sufism and Arabic.
فَأَجَابَ: الْمَذْهَبُ لَا يَجُوزُ إِلَّا جَافًّا مُنَقًّى
He answered: the school's position is that it is not allowed except as dry, cleaned dates;
هَذَا وَاللهَ اللهَ فِي حُسْنِ الْخُلُقِ مَعَ جَمِيعِ الْخَلْقِ
(Waṣiyya:) And now — God, God! — in good character with all creatures:

sections.teacher_note: Each line comes from a different kind of text: help children to look only for the frame words. The key says which kind each line is.

items.en: Line 1: which text type is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ١: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: A commentary on a ḥadīth. The frame is كَقَوْلِهِ … أَيْ …: “like his saying …, that is …”. The commentator quotes the ḥadīth and then explains it.

items.en: Line 2: which text type is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٢: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: A short ethical ḥadīth: a condition and its reward. مَنْ (“whoever”) + the deed, and then the result (سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ).

items.en: Line 3: which text type is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٣: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: Fiqh, a commentary on a ruling. The ruling verb لَا يُسَنُّ (“it is not recommended”) and a counted list (الْمَوَاضِعِ الْأَرْبَعَةِ, the four places).

items.en: Line 4: which text type is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٤: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: Creed, in prose: the three judgements. مَا يَسْتَحِيلُ and مَا يَجُوزُ (“what is impossible” and “what is possible”) with حَقِّهِ تَعَالَى.

items.en: Line 5: which text type is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٥: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: A litany: a prayer (يَا ذَا الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ، أَمِتْنَا …) with the count in brackets (7 times).

items.en: Line 6: which text type is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٦: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: Mawlid prose: rhymed phrases (sajʿ) in iḍāfa chains (أَشْرَفَ خَلْقِهِ وَأَجَلَّ عَبِيدِهِ) and a pausal ending (رَحْمَه).

items.en: Line 7: which text type is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٧: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: A qaṣīda: a line in two halves (the * between them) with the same rhyme and a prayer to God (فَمِنْكَ كُلُّ خِيرَةٍ).

items.en: Line 8: which text type is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٨: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: The sīra: a date measured from a famous event (حَادِثَةِ الْفِيلِ, the year of the Elephant), told in the third person.

items.en: Line 9: which text type is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٩: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: A biography (tarjama): he read with his teacher “in ḥadīth, tafsīr, taṣawwuf and Arabic”, a list of what a scholar studied.

items.en: Line 10: which text type is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ١٠: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: A fatwā: فَأَجَابَ (“and he answered”) opens the answer to a question; then the ruling (لَا يَجُوزُ إِلَّا …).

items.en: Line 11: which text type is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ١١: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: A waṣiyya (counsel to someone): the admonition فِي حُسْنِ الْخُلُقِ with the emphasis وَاللهَ اللهَ (“God, God!”).

items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
items.model: And whoever takes a road seeking knowledge on it, God makes easy for him by it a road to Paradise.

items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ.
items.model: And raising the hands is not recommended anywhere but these four places.

items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ السَّابِعَ.
items.model: From You is every good and every blessing upon us.

items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْعَاشِرَ.
items.model: He answered: the school's position is that it is not allowed except as dry, cleaned dates;

items.en: Line 6 has a chain of two nouns (an iḍāfa). Which is the first noun and which the second?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٦ فِيهِ إِضَافَةٌ. مَا الْمُضَافُ؟ وَمَا الْمُضَافُ إِلَيْهِ؟
items.model: أَجَلَّ is the first noun (“the greatest of”) and عَبِيدِهِ the second (“his servants”).

items.ar: فَمِنْكَ كُلُّ خِيرَةٍ * وَكُلُّ نِعْمَةٍ بِنَا
items.en: Line 7 has a * in the middle. What does it mark?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٧ فِيهِ * فِي الْوَسَطِ. عَلَى مَاذَا يَدُلُّ؟
items.model: The break between the two halves of the line of verse.

items.en: ★ Line 5 starts with يَا. What does it do, and what ending does the called word take here?
items.ar_q: ★ السَّطْرُ ٥ يَبْدَأُ بِـ«يَا». مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ؟ وَأَيُّ صُورَةٍ فِي «ذَا»؟
items.model: It calls: “O …”. ذَا is the five-noun form (Lesson 40): “O Possessor of …”.

جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَقَالَ: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ!
The boy came to the majlis and said: How beautiful this majlis is!
قَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَرَأَيْتُ الْحَبِيبَ.
He said to his mother: I came to the majlis and I saw the Habib.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ: عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّمٌ، تَعْلِيمٌ.
The boy wrote words from one root: ʿallama, muʿallim, taʿlīm.
And he wrote: sāfara, musāfir, safar.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى مِنْبَرِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمِحْرَابِهِ.
The boy looked at the minbar of the mosque and its miḥrāb.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ: أَنَا حَضْرَمِيٌّ مِنْ تَرِيمَ.
The boy said: I am a Ḥaḍramī, from Tarim.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ بِنَفْسِهِ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ وَوَجَدَ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ.
The boy looked in the dictionary by himself and found the meaning of the word.
ثُمَّ كَتَبَ الْجَذْرَ وَالْمَعْنَى فِي كِتَابِهِ.
Then he wrote the root and the meaning in his book.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ مَتْنًا صَغِيرًا.
The boy read a small matn (a short base text) with the Habib.
أَصْبَحَ الْمَتْنُ سَهْلًا لَكِنَّ الدَّرْسَ طَوِيلٌ.
The matn became easy, but the lesson is long.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الدَّرْسِ مُسْرِعًا وَجَلَسَ مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ.
The boy came to the lesson hurrying, and sat facing the qibla.
And the Habib was pleased with him.
ذَكَرَ الْوَلَدُ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا وَصَلَّى عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ ثَلَاثًا.
The boy remembered Allah a great deal and prayed for blessings on the Prophet ﷺ three times.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ مَرَّتَيْنِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ.
The boy read the lesson twice, seeking knowledge.
The Habib gave the boy a small book.
ظَنَّ الْوَلَدُ الْكِتَابَ صَعْبًا فَقَالَ: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ.
The boy thought the book difficult, so he said: There is no power and no strength except through Allah.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ أَرْكَانَ الْوُضُوءِ: الْأَوَّلُ النِّيَّةُ، وَالثَّانِي غَسْلُ الْوَجْهِ.
The boy wrote the pillars of the ablution: the first, the intention; and the second, washing the face.
وَالثَّالِثُ غَسْلُ الْيَدَيْنِ، وَالرَّابِعُ مَسْحُ بَعْضِ الرَّأْسِ.
And the third, washing the hands; and the fourth, wiping part of the head.
The boy read the wird in the morning.
ثُمَّ دَعَا: يَا رَبِّ، اِهْدِنَا وَاعْفُ عَنَّا، آمِينَ.
Then he made duʿāʾ: O my Lord, guide us and pardon us. Amen.
شَرِبَ الْوَلَدُ مِنْ مَاءِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمَا شَرِبَ إِلَّا مَاءً طَاهِرًا.
The boy drank from the water of the mosque, and he drank only pure water.
Neither its colour nor its taste had changed.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ اِسْمَ الشَّيْخِ عَلَى الْكِتَابِ: سَالِمُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ.
The boy read the shaykh’s name on the book: Salim son of Yusuf.
And his kunya is Abū Aḥmad.
رَغِبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْأَجْرِ وَرَغِبَ عَنِ الْإِثْمِ.
The boy desired knowledge and reward, and turned away from sin.
فَقَالَ لَهُ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا تَرْغَبْ فِي الدُّنْيَا.
So the Habib said to him: Do not set your desire on this world.
اِسْتَيْقَظَ الْوَلَدُ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ وَأَخَذَ السِّوَاكَ.
The boy woke up before dawn and took the siwāk.
Then he sat and strove in his wird.
The boy never missed the rawḥa.
يَحْضُرُ الْوَلَدُ الرَّوْحَةَ دَائِمًا وَهُوَ سَعِيدٌ جِدًّا.
The boy always attends the rawḥa, and he is very happy.
A letter arrived from the boy’s uncle.
بَدَأَ الْعَمُّ رِسَالَتَهُ: أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَاطْلُبِ الْعِلْمَ.
The uncle began his letter: Now then, seek knowledge.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ لِأُمِّهِ: هَذَا هُوَ الْكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُهُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy said to his mother: This is the book that I read with the Habib.
It is a small book that I read three times.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ لِيَحْضُرَ الدَّرْسَ.
The boy went to the mosque to attend the lesson.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لِيَتَعَلَّمْ كُلُّ طَالِبٍ كَيْ يَعْمَلَ بِعِلْمِهِ.
The Habib said: Let every student learn, so that he may act on his knowledge.
The Habib said: Whoever serves, learns.
وَإِذَا جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ فَهِمَ الدَّرْسَ.
And when the boy sat in the majlis, he understood the lesson.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ: وُلِدَ الْإِمَامُ فِي صَفَرَ سَنَةَ أَلْفٍ وَأَرْبَعٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ.
The boy wrote: The Imam was born in Ṣafar, in the year one thousand and forty-four.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ آيَةً ثُمَّ قَرَأَ تَفْسِيرَهَا.
The Habib read a verse, then read its commentary.
ثُمَّ قَالَ: الْحِكْمَةُ، أَيِ الْعِلْمُ وَالْعَمَلُ.
Then he said: Wisdom, that is, knowledge and action.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ الْإِسْنَادَ ثُمَّ الْمَتْنَ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ.
The Habib read the chain, then the matn: The Prophet ﷺ said: Religion is sincere counsel.
وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَعْنَى الْحَدِيثِ: عِمَادُ الدِّينِ النَّصِيحَةُ.
And the Habib said: The meaning of the ḥadīth: the pillar of religion is sincere counsel.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ.
The boy heard in the majlis: The Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever guides to good has a reward like that of the one who does it.
ثُمَّ دَلَّ الْوَلَدُ صَدِيقَهُ عَلَى الْمَجْلِسِ.
Then the boy guided his friend to the majlis.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ فِي الرَّوْحَةِ مِنَ الْمَتْنِ: يُسَنُّ رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ فِي أَرْبَعَةِ مَوَاضِعَ.
In the rawḥa the Habib read from the matn: Raising the hands is recommended in four places.
ثُمَّ سَأَلَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَا حُكْمُ رَفْعِ الْيَدَيْنِ؟ فَقَالَ الْوَلَدُ: سُنَّةٌ.
Then the Habib asked: What is the ruling on raising the hands? The boy said: A sunna.
قَرَأَتْ مَرْيَمُ عَقِيدَةً صَغِيرَةً فِي الْبَيْتِ وَسَمِعَهَا الْوَلَدُ.
Maryam read a small creed at home, and the boy listened to her.
She said: Allah exists; He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
قَالَ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ: يَا بُنَيَّ، عَلَيْكَ بِأَدَاءِ الْأَمَانَةِ وَإِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ فِيهَا.
The boy’s father said: My son, hold fast to returning what is entrusted, and beware of betraying it.
And hold fast to truthful speech and to keeping a promise.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ نَصِيحَةً طَوِيلَةً عَنِ التَّقْوَى.
The Habib read a long counsel about taqwā (God-consciousness).
وَمَعْنَاهَا: مَا مِنْ خَيْرٍ عَاجِلٍ وَلَا آجِلٍ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى سَبِيلٌ إِلَيْهِ.
And its meaning: There is no good, present or future, but taqwā is a road to it.
قَرَأَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ الرَّاتِبَ بَعْدَ الْعِشَاءِ وَحَضَرَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَهُمْ.
The people of Tarim read the Rātib after ʿIshāʾ, and the boy attended with them.
وَقَالُوا: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ ثَلَاثًا.
And they said: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created (three times).
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْمَوْلِدِ اِجْتَمَعَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
On the night of the mawlid the people of Tarim gathered in the mosque.
وَقَرَأَ الْجَمِيعُ الْمَوْلِدَ وَذَكَرُوا جَمَالَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وَكَمَالَهُ.
And everyone read the mawlid and they mentioned the beauty of the Prophet ﷺ and his perfection.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ قَصِيدَةً فِي مَدْحِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.
The boy heard in the majlis a qaṣīda in praise of the Prophet ﷺ.
And in every verse there is a first half and a second half.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ سِيرَةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ: وُلِدَ فِي مَكَّةَ وَنَشَأَ يَتِيمًا وَكَفَلَهُ جَدُّهُ.
The boy read the life of the Prophet ﷺ: He was born in Mecca, grew up an orphan, and his grandfather took him in his care.
So the boy loved the Prophet ﷺ even more.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ رِسَالَةً مِنْ رَسَائِلِ الْإِمَامِ.
The boy copied out a letter from the letters of the Imam.
وَكَانَ فِي أَوَّلِهَا: وَبَعْدُ، وَفِي آخِرِهَا: وَالسَّلَامُ.
At its beginning was: “And now”, and at its end: “And peace”.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: إِنَّ لِلْعَبْدِ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ رِزْقًا مَعْلُومًا.
The Habib said, in meaning: The servant has in every moment a known provision.
وَكَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ ذَلِكَ وَقَالَ: نَفَعَنَا اللَّهُ بِهِ.
And the boy wrote that down and said: May Allah benefit us through him.
سَأَلَتْ فَاطِمَةُ: هَلْ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يَبِيعَ الرَّجُلُ الرُّطَبَ فِي السُّوقِ؟
Fatima asked: Is it allowed for a man to sell fresh dates in the market?
The Habib was asked, and he answered: Yes, it is allowed.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَتْنِ عَنِ الْإِعْرَابِ: وَأَقْسَامُهُ أَرْبَعَةٌ: رَفْعٌ وَنَصْبٌ وَخَفْضٌ وَجَزْمٌ.
The boy read in the matn about iʿrāb: Its kinds are four: rafʿ, naṣb, khafḍ and jazm.
وَعَرَفَ الْوَلَدُ أَنَّ الضَّمَّةَ عَلَامَةُ الرَّفْعِ.
And the boy knew that the ḍamma is the sign of rafʿ.
اِسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى تَسْجِيلِ دَرْسٍ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy listened to a recording of a lesson by the Habib.
And the boy understood all the words of the Habib.
